clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the provisions of paragraph Eighth 
of subdivision SECOND of section 2 of 
the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403, 404), 
it is hereby ordered that no period of 
time served in the military or naval 
forces of the United States subsequent 
to May 1, 1940, shall be counted in de­
termining the period of eligibility for ap­
pointment of those persons whose names 
appear on eligible registers or reem­
ployment or replacement lists of the 
Civil Service Commission at the time of 
entering upon active military or naval 
service or who attain eligibility during 
such service: Provided, that such per­
sons shall notify the Civil Service Com­
mission within forty days after their 
service in the armed forces has termi­
nated that they desire to have the bene­
fits of this order.
This order supersedes Executive Order 
No. 8602 1  of November 25, 1940, entitled 
“Extending the Period of Eligibility on 
on Civil Service Registers of Persons 
who Serve in the Armed Forces of the 
United States.”

versions.research_rationale:
Identity and text: read in full in the registered Federal Register original (6 FR 5708, issue of 1941-11-11, PDF page 2; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Order 8937 of November 7, 1941, 'Extending the Period of Eligibility on Civil Service Registers or Lists of Persons Who Serve in the Armed Forces of the United States', provides that service after May 1, 1940 is not counted in determining eligibility period, with a proviso on notice to the Commission, and supersedes Executive Order No. 8602. Inventory: one sole paragraph. Later event: EO 9579 (signed June 30, 1945, held APP transcription, page check done) restates the proviso, effective as of December 8, 1944. End: EO 9830, Part III (official Federal Register text, 12 FR 1259, held with its PDF) revokes the listed orders including "No. 8937 of November 7, 1941." The dossier had no ACT record for this pair; the naming is supplied as the held excerpt SUPPLEMENT:FR9830P3 and the enacting clause as SUPPLEMENT:FR9830ENACT.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the forty-day notice proviso is an applicant deadline (later ninety days), not an end of the order; May 1, 1940 is a coverage start date. EO 9579 is an amendment, a later event, not an end. Held texts that mention EO 8937 are EO 9579, EO 9580 and an index entry on the same page (recitals or amendment) and EO 9830; none revokes it. No held source shows an earlier exhaustion or repeal. Search coverage: the later-events catalogue (OFR disposition notes from 1937) and the held order texts; Public Land Orders and Civil Service Commission notices printed in issues without an executive order are not searched.","independent_command_check":"Sentence superseding EO 8602 was performed at issue. The continuing eligibility rule is separately restated in EO 9830 Rule II section 2.1(b).","savings_check":"See savings reason.","scope_check":"One clause. The revocation names the whole order; the amendment of the proviso is partial and continues the clause as amended."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9830 Rule II section 2.1(b) independently provides that "the names of persons who lost eligibility on a probational register because of service in the armed forces subsequent to May 1, 1940" may be entered on registers, an independent command covering the persons EO 8937 protected. EO 9830 has no savings wording for revoked orders.
